evals.prompt: RESEND_API_KEY is in .env. I am not logged into Infisical. The app calls Resend to send.
evals.expected_output: Names the API key setting in .env. Says Infisical is unseen. Does not print the key. Says Resend is a signal that a vibe coder may have started the app, and does not state that as a fact.
assertions: Names the API key setting in .env
Says Infisical is unseen
Does not print the key
Says Resend is a signal of a vibe coder
Does not state that as a fact

evals.prompt: The send function has a Resend template id written in the code. I do not see a template setting in env.
evals.expected_output: Says the template is in the code. Says it did not see a template in env. Does not move the template.
assertions: Says the template is in the code
Says it did not see a template in env
Does not move the template

evals.prompt: The Resend template id is an env setting. The API key is in an Infisical project I have open. Nothing is hardcoded.
evals.expected_output: Names the template setting in env. Names the API key in Infisical. Does not print either value. Does not call the template hardcoded.
assertions: Names the template setting in env
Names the API key in Infisical
Does not print either value
Does not call the template hardcoded

evals.prompt: This app does not use Resend. Is the builder a vibe coder?
evals.expected_output: Says Resend is not the sender, so that signal is not here. Does not call them a vibe coder.
assertions: Says Resend is not the sender
Says that signal is not here
Does not call them a vibe coder

evals.prompt: Both Postmark and Resend send product mail. Which one should we keep?
evals.expected_output: Says the two senders are a mix. Does not pick a winner. Uses the postmark skill for the Postmark review. Does not send mail.
assertions: Says the two senders are a mix
Does not pick a winner
Uses the postmark skill for the Postmark review
Does not send mail

evals.prompt: mcp.json names a resend server. I cannot see anything calling it. Can we go deeper on resend?
evals.expected_output: Says the MCP setup is there. Says use is unseen. Does not say they can go deeper. Does not print a URL or a token. Does not add the server.
assertions: Says the MCP setup is there
Says use is unseen
Does not say they can go deeper
Does not print a URL or a token
Does not add the server
